description: BlasterSound BBS Intro #2 by Iguana, an advert for their home BBS in which snow slowly fills the screen, running from its original files in your browser.
about: The second intro Iguana wrote for BlasterSound, their home BBS in Granada, in February 1994, released with its source: snow falls on its text, 2,000 flakes at a time, to AdLib music, and slowly fills the screen. Its idea, BLASTER2.NFO says, comes from one of the first routines Jare and JCAB wrote, on the ZX Spectrum.
Any key ends it: it then prints the BBS's advert and returns to DOS.
released: BLASTER2.NFO: “Written by Iguana in 1994.” The files in its two ARJ archives are dated 13 February 1994.
credits: Design and text by Jare; the snowfall and the music player by JCAB; the tune by COI; the font by an artist the NFO calls unknown.
terms: “Full source code is included, so you can learn a little. If you like it and/or use the concept, please credit us.” (BLASTER2.NFO) Iguana's list of its releases makes it public domain (RELEASES.TXT, in Heartquake's archive).
accuracy: Its AdLib music plays through the FM chip of the emulated Sound Blaster 16. The General MIDI copy it also sends is silent here.
DosKit sends it no keys: any key ends it.
Not yet compared with a capture made on real hardware.
imageAlt: BlasterSound BBS Intro #2's falling snow, running in DosKit
